purpose: Restructured, capability-based inventory of every addressable PostgreSQL database environment relevant to this repository. Supersedes environment-topology-v1.json, which the independent audit at /opt/worker/report/codex-topology-presign-2026-08-29.md judged HOLD for two reasons: (1) it omitted a materialized host PostgreSQL 17/main cluster and nine database-creation scripts targeting it, and (2) it mixed physical database identity, access/lifecycle mechanism, and potential-environment-generator into one flat environments[] array. This file splits those into clusters[] (physical DB server identity), databases[] (concrete databases, each owned by exactly one cluster), and mechanisms[] (creation/access/lifecycle paths, each pointing at the cluster/database it acts on).
constraints_honored: read-only everywhere: no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL issued by this task against any of the discovered databases
local dev compose: only `docker compose start postgres` on the already-existing, previously-exited container (no create/recreate/down/-v), matching the precedent already accepted in v1

host PostgreSQL 17/main cluster: read-only `psql` via `sudo -n -u postgres` (peer auth), used only for `\l`, `information_schema.tables`, `pg_roles`, and `SELECT count(*) FROM pages` inside `BEGIN TRANSACTION READ ONLY; ... COMMIT;` where applicable
kkso: read-only only (`docker compose ps`, `psql -c '\l'`, `SELECT count(*) FROM schema_migrations`, `SELECT count(*) FROM pages` in a read-only transaction); no restart, no config change
no git commit / push / stash performed

clusters.description: podman-compose project 'openpr' (default project name = repo root directory basename; no `name:` override in docker-compose.yml, no COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME in .env/.env.example), service 'postgres', container 'openpr_postgres_1', image docker.io/library/postgres:16, persistent named volume 'openpr_pgdata'
clusters.evidence: `podman inspect openpr_postgres_1` labels: com.docker.compose.project=openpr, com.docker.compose.service=postgres, com.docker.compose.project.config_files=docker-compose.yml. Container observed 'Exited (0) 26 minutes ago (healthy)' at scan start, started (not recreated) via `docker compose start postgres` for read-only querying, matching v1's precedent.
clusters.persistence: named volume 'openpr_pgdata' survives `docker compose down` (without -v) and host reboot by construction

clusters.description: Directly-installed PostgreSQL 17 cluster 'main', managed by systemd unit postgresql@17-main.service, independent of any container/compose stack. This is the cluster v1 omitted entirely.
clusters.evidence: `systemctl status postgresql@17-main.service` -> active (running) since 2026-08-26 14:23:23 EDT, Main PID 1183 /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin/postgres -D /var/lib/postgresql/17/main. `ss -tlnp` confirms LISTEN on 0.0.0.0:5366 and [::]:5366, owning process postgres/1183. `sudo -n cat /etc/postgresql/17/main/postgresql.conf` confirms data_directory and port=5366 match the systemd process.
clusters.auth: pg_hba.conf: 'local all postgres peer', 'local all all peer', 'host all all 127.0.0.1/32 scram-sha-256', 'host all all ::1/128 scram-sha-256', 'host all all 0.0.0.0/0 md5' -- reachable both via local unix-socket peer auth (used by the 9 smoke scripts through `sudo -n -u postgres psql`) and via password auth from any host reaching this VM's IP on 5366.
clusters.database_enumeration_method: `sudo -n -u postgres psql -p 5366 -d postgres -c '\\l'` (superuser, lists every database on the cluster, not name-filtered)
